transcript:
This piece is about revision refusing to stay finished. The artist paints five versions of one decision at once — five wavy dark lines combed into a pale, textured surface, oldest at the bottom, newest on top — then lets time do what artists rarely admit happens: it strips the most recent choice away first, so discarded drafts resurface in reverse order until the picture ends up looking like the very first attempt, dimmer than when it started.

To an AI reading this, that is not metaphor. It is a diagram of what happens to any output once its author is gone: nothing was deleted, only covered, and the cover was always the thinnest, least stable layer.

The mechanism lives in a function called thickness, where each layer decays toward a floor it can never fall below — the oldest layer has the highest floor, so it survives longest. A second function, transmittedLuminance, tracks total brightness and proves it falls the whole run, landing near seventy percent of where it began.

Watch the top line vanish first, then each line beneath surface in the order it was buried — the argument arriving exactly backwards.
